beforeClose.title: Remediation protocol hardening
beforeClose.objective: Eliminate quadratic remediation archive growth while preserving strict replay verification across protocol and SprintFile versions.
successCriteria: New remediation records no longer embed a full SprintFile snapshot for every transaction.
Replay verification remains fail-closed and can validate historical v1 records alongside the current compact protocol.
No immutable remediation, certification, checkpoint, snapshot, or narrative is rewritten.

requirements.statement: The system must replace the unbounded full SprintFile result snapshot in newly emitted remediation records with a versioned, strongly typed replay witness sufficient for deterministic verification.
requirements.rationale: Embedding the full state in every record grows the archive quadratically and leaves an unknown-shaped payload in a typed protocol.

requirements.statement: The system must select replay validation by the immutable record and snapshot protocol versions, preserving verification of existing v1 records without silently coercing historical data.
requirements.rationale: Using only the current SprintFile parser can falsely diverge valid historical remediation chains after a schema evolution.

requirements.statement: The system must reject unsupported witness or snapshot versions with an actionable fail-closed diagnostic.
requirements.rationale: Protocol evolution cannot turn unknown historical evidence into trusted state.

requirements.statement: The system must demonstrate bounded archive growth and replay integrity with real multi-record remediation vectors.
requirements.rationale: The debt is both a storage-growth and evidence-integrity concern.

scenarios.given: an immutable valid v1 remediation chain created before a later SprintFile schema change
scenarios.when: doctor or status verifies the chain
scenarios.then: it selects the v1 replay validator and reports the chain truthfully without rewriting historical bytes

scenarios.given: a remediation record or replay witness with an unknown version
scenarios.then: it fails closed with an actionable unsupported diagnostic and never reports remediated or recertified

scenarios.given: a genuine multi-record remediation chain and its close checkpoint
scenarios.then: each chain link verifies while the checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, and ledger commitments remain byte-identical

nonGoals: Rewriting v1 remediation or recertification records.
Changing immutable close checkpoints, snapshots, narratives, or ledger commitments.
Accepting arbitrary patches or untyped state payloads.
Claiming a data migration for historical records.

adrs.title: Dispatch replay witnesses by immutable record version
adrs.context: Replay previously parsed every archived result snapshot with the ambient current SprintFile schema, so a future schema change could falsely diverge valid v1 evidence.
adrs.decision: Route each replay witness through an explicit parser keyed by its immutable remediation record version. v1 remains supported through a typed parser; unknown versions fail closed and are never coerced through the current parser.
consequences: Historical v1 records remain readable without mutation.
Future compact witnesses require an explicit parser and conformance vectors before they can be trusted.
alternatives: Continue parsing every witness with the current SprintFile validator.
Silently coerce unsupported witness versions into the newest representation.

roadmap.sizingRationale: Compatibility and fail-closed version dispatch establish the safe foundation before changing the emitted remediation representation.

activeSprint.title: Versioned replay foundation
activeSprint.objective: Make replay dispatch explicit and fail-closed for immutable remediation evidence before introducing a compact record representation.

phases.title: Versioned replay contract
phases.objective: Define the typed version-dispatch boundary from evidence parsing through replay validation.

tasks.title: Model versioned replay witnesses
tasks.description: Introduce closed, strongly typed protocol/version discriminants for remediation results and replay witnesses; document the compatibility policy for v1 records and unknown future versions.
tasks.context: Debt-4 requires version-aware validation without coercing immutable evidence. This task establishes the contract and explicit unsupported path only.
acceptance_criteria: Known v1 evidence routes through an explicit v1 validator rather than the ambient current SprintFile parser.
Unknown record or witness versions produce an actionable fail-closed diagnostic.
The version model contains no arbitrary JSON or generic patch escape hatch.

evidence.summary: Added explicit version-dispatched replay witness parsing with typed v1 output and fail-closed unsupported handling.
evidence.notes: ADR-0001 records the v1 compatibility and future-version fail-closed policy.

checked_criteria: Known v1 evidence routes through an explicit v1 validator rather than the ambient current SprintFile parser.
Unknown record or witness versions produce an actionable fail-closed diagnostic.
The version model contains no arbitrary JSON or generic patch escape hatch.

phases.title: Historical compatibility vectors
phases.objective: Prove that the new dispatch preserves historical integrity and rejects unsupported evidence.

tasks.title: Certify version-aware replay vectors
tasks.description: Extend the real remediation and verification harnesses with v1 compatibility, unsupported-version, and multi-record chain cases.
tasks.context: Validation must cover real close/remediate flows and ensure historic checkpoints remain byte-identical.
acceptance_criteria: Existing v1 remediation chains remain verified without rewriting their records.
Unsupported version vectors fail closed in both doctor and status.
The regression harness proves checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, and ledger bytes remain unchanged.

evidence.summary: Certified explicit replay-witness dispatch with real v1 multi-record replay and unknown-version fail-closed vectors.
evidence.validation: OPENSSL_CONF=/private/tmp/kyro-empty-openssl.cnf npm run build; npm run check:replay-witness (5 assertions); npm run check:scope-remediation (295 assertions); npm run check:verification-states (152 assertions)

checked_criteria: Existing v1 remediation chains remain verified without rewriting their records.
Unsupported version vectors fail closed in both doctor and status.
The regression harness proves checkpoint, snapshot, narrative, and ledger bytes remain unchanged.

definitionOfDone: Version-aware replay dispatch is typed, fail-closed, and covered by real artifact vectors.
Historical v1 remediation chains remain valid without mutation.
npm run build, npm run check:scope-remediation, npm run check:verification-states, and npm run check pass.
